reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The new test unconditionally runs a `/bin/sh` fixture and uses a Unix-only PATH separator, causing `go test ./router/openwrt` to fail on Windows without a platform skip.
1 open issue - [Skip Unix-only fixture test on Windows](https://github.com/nextdns/nextdns/pull/1157#discussion_r4572544755) · New
What changed in this PR This PR fixes an OpenWrt configuration case where dnsmasq can compete with NextDNS for port 53 when caching is enabled. It addresses the explicit-port case, not a confirmed cause of #1139. **Changes:** - Set `SetPort0` after successfully deleting and committing an explicit dnsmasq port of 53, leaving custom ports unchanged. - Add a regression test using a fake UCI executable and a no-op dnsmasq restart. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `router/​openwrt/​setup.go` | Ensure generated configuration disables dnsmasq DNS after removing explicit port 53. | | `router/​openwrt/​setup_port_test.go` | Test that the explicit-port case generates `port=0`. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: This test unconditionally runs a `/bin/sh` fixture and uses a Unix-only PATH separator, so `go test ./router/openwrt` fails on Windows instead of testing the package. Please skip it on Windows, as `fakeLegacyUCI` already does in `relay_test.go`, before creating or executing the fixture.
